# The immune response

## Innate and adaptive immunity

The innate immune system responds quickly and in the same way to many different pathogens. Its defences include skin, inflammation and white blood cells called phagocytes. The adaptive immune system responds more slowly but targets a specific pathogen. Adaptive immunity relies on lymphocytes, which are B cells and T cells.

## Memory

B cells produce antibodies that bind to a specific antigen. After an infection some B cells and T cells remain as memory cells. Memory cells let the body respond faster if the same pathogen returns. Vaccines work by exposing the immune system to a harmless form of an antigen so that memory cells form.
